Optional Checklists for Practice Sessions

Prepare and review educational exercises without prescribing a professional routine or profitable outcome.

By Anuga Weerasinghe

Published by TradeHQ, created by Anuga Weerasinghe. Publisher background and editorial approach. No independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.

Source check: 2026-10-18. Reviewed claimed routine durations and simulator limitations; no duration treated as an empirically validated standard.

QUICK ANSWER
Optional Checklists for Practice Sessions?

Prepare and review educational exercises without prescribing a professional routine or profitable outcome. Use a checklist only when it assists a defined educational question. Any duration, time of day or review frequency is optional.

A checklist is an organisational tool

A checklist may help a learner remember what an exercise is meant to test. It is not a proven method for increasing financial returns and there is no universal pre-market, hourly or end-of-day schedule suitable for everyone.

Before a virtual exercise

Write a narrow objective: for example, calculate a trade fee from an assumed price and quantity, or distinguish a spot quote from a futures-contract example. Record whether the numbers come from dated market observations or are invented for teaching. It is fine to spend a session learning without placing an order.

During the exercise

If the original question changes, note the change rather than silently replacing earlier assumptions. A learner can pause or end an exercise at any point. TradeHQ places manual market orders in supported spot instruments; writing a stop or a take-profit on a checklist does not create one.

After the exercise

Compare original assumptions with the observed virtual result. For example, 10 units at a hypothetical $50 price have $500 notional; a 0.1% virtual transaction fee would be $0.50. Ask whether transaction costs were included and whether a later price is comparable by timestamp and source.

Design your own review cadence

Some learners may prefer a short end-of-session note; others may periodically review multiple examples. Neither 30-minute preparation nor a 60-second hourly check nor a 20-minute closing ritual is a professional standard established by this course. The quantity of time spent does not prove better decision quality.

Distinguish participation from outcomes

Completing a quiz or maintaining an educational streak reflects participation under feature rules. It does not validate a trading system, require frequent trading or establish higher expected returns.

(Educational only — not financial advice. TradeHQ offers $100,000 virtual cash for supported spot instruments. Options contracts, Greeks, futures margin and settlement are conceptual exercises; the simulator does not execute them.)

KEY TAKEAWAYS
Use a checklist only when it assists a defined educational question.
Any duration, time of day or review frequency is optional.
Record how prices, assumptions and fees were obtained.
Completing a routine does not imply profitability or the need to trade.
Check Your Understanding

Answer all 4 questions to complete this lesson.

1. What duration must a pre-session checklist have?
Exactly 30 minutesAn hourNo universal durationExactly five minutes
2. Does a written stop price create a resting order in TradeHQ?
No, virtual orders are manual market ordersYes, alwaysOnly after 20 minutesOnly with an options contract
3. Why record source and observation time?
It guarantees a fillIt can clarify which information was availableIt proves market directionIt increases expected profit
4. What does a learning streak measure?
Trading expertiseFuture profitLow drawdownParticipation under the feature's rules
Submit & complete lesson
Answer notes
What duration must a pre-session checklist have? Options: Exactly 30 minutes; An hour; No universal duration; Exactly five minutes. Correct answer: No universal duration. Why: Checklists are optional learning tools, not a timed professional standard.
Does a written stop price create a resting order in TradeHQ? Options: No, virtual orders are manual market orders; Yes, always; Only after 20 minutes; Only with an options contract. Correct answer: No, virtual orders are manual market orders. Why: A worksheet assumption is not an executable resting order.
Why record source and observation time? Options: It guarantees a fill; It can clarify which information was available; It proves market direction; It increases expected profit. Correct answer: It can clarify which information was available. Why: A source timestamp helps interpret an observed price without promising any outcome.
What does a learning streak measure? Options: Trading expertise; Future profit; Low drawdown; Participation under the feature's rules. Correct answer: Participation under the feature's rules. Why: Participation is not an investment-performance measure.

Use $100,000 in virtual cash to practise supported spot instruments and general habits such as recording a trade thesis. Options contracts, Greeks, futures margin and daily settlement are conceptual exercises: calculate their examples in a worksheet, because TradeHQ does not execute derivatives contracts. Educational simulation only — not financial advice.
